hook.text: You turn the hot water tap in a shower. Nothing happens for ten seconds. You turn harder.

buildup.text: Delays are gaps between an action and its effect. Every system has them. They cause overreaction and oscillation.

discovery.text: The beer game demonstrates this: small demand changes amplify into wild swings up the supply chain because of delays.

twist.text: Delays cannot be eliminated, only managed. Patience and anticipation beat frantic adjustment every time.

climax.text: When you act and see no change, wait before acting again. The system may be responding—it just has not shown you yet.

punchline.text: No change yet does not mean no effect. Systems have delays.

quiz.question: What common mistake do delays cause in systems?
options: People overreact because they don't see immediate results and adjust too much
